lesson_scope: Complex conjugate root theorem for polynomials with real coefficients: forming quadratic factors, cubic and quartic factorisation via polynomial division, determining unknown polynomial coefficients, and geometric configurations of polynomial roots in the Argand plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Forming real quadratic factor from conjugate roots.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming quadratic factor from conjugate pair.

walkthrough.text:
Identify conjugate root:
$$\text{Since coefficients are real, the other root is } \overline{2 - 3\mathrm{i}} = 2 + 3\mathrm{i}$$

Form monic quadratic factor:
$$(z - (2 - 3\mathrm{i}))(z - (2 + 3\mathrm{i})) = (z - 2)^2 + 3^2 = z^2 - 4z + 13$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Real root of cubic given conjugate pair.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding real root of cubic.

walkthrough.text:
State conjugate roots:
$$\text{Conjugate roots are } z_1 = 1 + 2\mathrm{i} \text{ and } z_2 = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$$

Apply sum of roots relation:
$$z_1 + z_2 + z_3 = -(-5) = 5 \implies (1 + 2\mathrm{i}) + (1 - 2\mathrm{i}) + z_3 = 5 \implies z_3 = 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses sum of roots $2 + \alpha = 5$ or product $5\alpha = 15$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Finding unknown coefficient of cubic from complex root.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding unknown coefficient in cubic.

walkthrough.text:
Find real root using constant term:
$$(1^2 + 3^2)\alpha = 10 \implies 10\alpha = 10 \implies \alpha = 1$$

Find $a$ using sum of roots:
$$-a = (1 + 3\mathrm{i}) + (1 - 3\mathrm{i}) + 1 = 3 \implies a = -3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds real root $\alpha = 1$ via product of roots $10\alpha = 10$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Polar root and conjugate in quadratic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Conjugate of polar root and constant term.

walkthrough.text:
State conjugate root in polar form:
$$\bar{z}_1 = 4\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}}$$

Calculate constant term $c$:
$$c = z_1 \bar{z}_1 = |z_1|^2 = 4^2 = 16$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving cubic with pure imaginary root.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cubic with pure imaginary root.

hints: Divide by $z^2 + 9$ to get linear factor $(2z + 3) \implies z = -\frac{3}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = \mathrm{i}y$ and equate real and imaginary parts:
$$-3y^2 + 27 = 0 \implies y^2 = 9 \implies y = 3 \quad (\text{since } y > 0)$$
$$\text{Imaginary roots: } 3\mathrm{i} \text{ and } -3\mathrm{i}$$

Factorise cubic by dividing by $z^2 + 9$:
$$2z^3 + 3z^2 + 18z + 27 = (z^2 + 9)(2z + 3) = 0 \implies z = -\frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Three roots: } 3\mathrm{i}, -3\mathrm{i}, -\frac{3}{2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $\mathrm{i}y$ and equates parts to find $y = 3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Quartic with two conjugate pairs forming rectangle in Argand plane.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Quartic roots forming symmetric geometric figure.

hints: Vertices $(\pm 2, \pm 3)$ form a rectangle of sides $4$ and $6$.

walkthrough.text:
Solve both quadratic factors:
$$z^2 - 4z + 13 = 0 \implies z = 2 \pm 3\mathrm{i}$$
$$z^2 + 4z + 13 = 0 \implies z = -2 \pm 3\mathrm{i}$$

Analyse geometry:
$$\text{Vertices: } (2, 3), (2, -3), (-2, -3), (-2, 3)$$
$$\text{Sides are parallel to axes with lengths } 4 \text{ and } 6, \text{ forming a rectangle.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves both quadratics to obtain $2 \pm 3\mathrm{i}$ and $-2 \pm 3\mathrm{i}$.
Explains vertices form a rectangle with side lengths $4$ and $6$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Finding third root and coefficients of cubic polynomial.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding quadratic factor and real root of cubic.

hints: Linear factor is $(z + 3)$ since $5 \times 3 = 15$. Third root is $-3$.

walkthrough.text:
Form quadratic factor:
$$(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}))(z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})) = (z - 1)^2 + 4 = z^2 - 2z + 5$$

Find third root from constant term:
$$(z + \alpha)(z^2 - 2z + 5) \implies 5\alpha = 15 \implies \alpha = 3 \implies z_3 = -3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding polynomial coefficients by expansion.

walkthrough.text:
Expand factored polynomial:
$$(z + 3)(z^2 - 2z + 5) = z^3 - 2z^2 + 5z + 3z^2 - 6z + 15 = z^3 + z^2 - z + 15$$

Equate coefficients:
$$a = 1, \quad b = -1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Cubic root finding and isosceles triangle area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding complex roots of cubic with known real root.

walkthrough.text:
Solve quadratic factor:
$$z = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 40}}{2} = 1 \pm 3\mathrm{i} \implies z_2 = 1 + 3\mathrm{i}, \quad z_3 = 1 - 3\mathrm{i}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving triangle is isosceles and finding its area.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate side lengths:
$$AB = \sqrt{(5 - 1)^2 + (0 - 3)^2} = 5$$
$$AC = \sqrt{(5 - 1)^2 + (0 - (-3))^2} = 5$$
$$BC = |3 - (-3)| = 6$$
$$\text{Since } AB = AC = 5, \text{ triangle } ABC \text{ is isosceles.}$$

Calculate area:
$$\text{Altitude from } A(5, 0) \text{ to vertical line } x = 1 \text{ is } h = 5 - 1 = 4$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(6)(4) = 12$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes triangle is isosceles since $AB = AC = 5$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Quartic factorisation into real quadratics and argument comparison.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Factoring quartic into two real quadratics.

walkthrough.text:
Form first quadratic factor:
$$(z - (2 + \mathrm{i}))(z - (2 - \mathrm{i})) = (z - 2)^2 + 1 = z^2 - 4z + 5$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all four roots and comparing arguments.

walkthrough.text:
Solve second factor $z^2 - 2z + 5 = 0$:
$$z = 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i} \implies \text{Four roots: } 2 \pm \mathrm{i}, \quad 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i}$$

Compare principal arguments:
$$\arg(1 + 2\mathrm{i}) = \arctan(2) \approx 1.107 \text{ rad}$$
$$\arg(2 + \mathrm{i}) = \arctan(0.5) \approx 0.464 \text{ rad}$$
$$\text{The root with the greatest principal argument is } 1 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves second quadratic factor to obtain $1 \pm 2\mathrm{i}$.
Identifies $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$ as having the greatest argument.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Determining coefficients and solving quartic equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coefficients of quartic polynomial from complex root.

walkthrough.text:
Form quadratic factor:
$$(z - (1 - 3\mathrm{i}))(z - (1 + 3\mathrm{i})) = (z - 1)^2 + 9 = z^2 - 2z + 10$$

Express $P(z)$ as product of quadratic factors:
$$P(z) = (z^2 - 2z + 10)(2z^2 + cz + 2)$$
$$\text{Linear coefficient: } 10c - 4 = -24 \implies c = -2$$
$$a = c - 4 = -6, \quad b = 22 - 2c = 26$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving second quadratic to list all roots.

walkthrough.text:
State conjugate root:
$$z_2 = 1 + 3\mathrm{i}$$

Solve second factor $2z^2 - 2z + 2 = 0$:
$$z^2 - z + 1 = 0 \implies z = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4}}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Other three roots: } 1 + 3\mathrm{i}, \quad \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{i}, \quad \frac{1}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Lists all other three roots in exact Cartesian form.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Quartic roots, polar forms, and powers.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quartic polynomial into 4 Cartesian roots.

hints: Conjugate root is $1 - \mathrm{i}$, quadratic factor is $z^2 - 2z + 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Form quadratic factor for $1 \pm \mathrm{i}$:
$$(z - (1 + \mathrm{i}))(z - (1 - \mathrm{i})) = (z - 1)^2 + 1 = z^2 - 2z + 2$$

Divide $P(z)$ by $z^2 - 2z + 2$:
$$z^4 - 2z^3 + 6z^2 - 8z + 8 = (z^2 - 2z + 2)(z^2 + 4) = 0$$
$$\text{Four roots: } 1 + \mathrm{i}, \quad 1 - \mathrm{i}, \quad 2\mathrm{i}, \quad -2\mathrm{i}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Converting roots to polar form and evaluating powers.

walkthrough.text:
Convert roots to polar form:
$$1 \pm \mathrm{i} = \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{e}^{\pm\frac{\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}}, \quad \pm 2\mathrm{i} = 2\mathrm{e}^{\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}$$

Evaluate eighth powers:
$$(1 \pm \mathrm{i})^8 = (\sqrt{2})^8 \mathrm{e}^{\pm 2\pi\mathrm{i}} = 16 > 0$$
$$(\pm 2\mathrm{i})^8 = 2^8 \mathrm{e}^{\pm 4\pi\mathrm{i}} = 256 > 0$$
$$\text{All eighth powers are strictly positive real numbers.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes all eighth powers are positive real numbers.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Cubic with polar root and parameter determination.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Converting polar root and forming quadratic factor.

walkthrough.text:
Convert $w$ to Cartesian form:
$$w = 3\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + \mathrm{i}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} + \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\mathrm{i}$$
$$\bar{w} = 3\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\mathrm{i}$$

Form quadratic factor:
$$(z - w)(z - \bar{w}) = z^2 - 2\operatorname{Re}(w)z + |w|^2 = z^2 - 3\sqrt{2}z + 9$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding third root and determining coefficients k and m.

walkthrough.text:
Equate coefficients with $(z - \alpha)(z^2 - 3\sqrt{2}z + 9)$:
$$\text{Linear coefficient: } 9 + 3\sqrt{2}\alpha = 18 \implies 3\sqrt{2}\alpha = 9 \implies \alpha = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$$

Compute $k$ and $m$:
$$k = -(3\sqrt{2} + \alpha) = -\left(3\sqrt{2} + \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
$$m = -9\alpha = -9\left(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = -\frac{27\sqrt{2}}{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Quartic roots forming isosceles trapezium, diagonals, and area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all four roots of quartic.

walkthrough.text:
Form first quadratic factor:
$$(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}))(z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})) = z^2 - 2z + 5$$

Divide $P(z)$ by $z^2 - 2z + 5$:
$$z^4 - 8z^3 + 42z^2 - 80z + 125 = (z^2 - 2z + 5)(z^2 - 6z + 25) = 0$$
$$z^2 - 6z + 25 = 0 \implies z = 3 \pm 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Four roots: } 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i}, \quad 3 \pm 4\mathrm{i}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is isosceles trapezium.

hints: Isosceles trapezium since parallel sides are $4, 8$ and legs are equal ($2\sqrt{2}$).

walkthrough.text:
Calculate parallel vertical side lengths:
$$AD = |2 - (-2)| = 4, \quad BC = |4 - (-4)| = 8$$
$$\text{Both segments lie on vertical lines } x = 1 \text{ and } x = 3, \text{ so } AD \parallel BC.$$

Calculate non-parallel side lengths:
$$AB = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (4 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 4} = 2\sqrt{2}$$
$$DC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (-4 - (-2))^2} = \sqrt{4 + 4} = 2\sqrt{2}$$
$$\text{Since } AB = DC, \text{ the quadrilateral is an isosceles trapezium.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Computes vertical parallel side lengths $AD = 4$ and $BC = 8$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating diagonal lengths and area of trapezium.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate area of trapezium:
$$\text{Perpendicular height } h = 3 - 1 = 2$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(4 + 8)(2) = 12$$
